ideas.title: The island tips
ideas.critique: Crowd-triggered island-wide event with a scramble payoff is the familiar gather-and-react shape. The whole world leaning, with horizon tilt and rolling props, changes what the island is physically, and the overshoot rocking is a strong, visible hook.

ideas.title: Low tide, and the sandbar
ideas.critique: A tide cycle that opens a new place is a real permanent world mechanic, but it is a scheduled event with a race and retrieval, which is a familiar romp shape. The stranded slow friend is a nice beat; sea-level change is partly predictable from goals about water.

ideas.title: I molt
ideas.critique: Changing Lumi's own body over an hour, with feathers becoming bedding, is a new kind of change: slow, embarrassing and persistent. It is a body change rather than a gathering, which sets it apart from nearly every recent post; the risk is that it reads as a still.

ideas.title: Full-moon gravity
ideas.critique: A physics rule on a cycle is an ambient behaviour change, the same form as Lights out, and goal 3 hands over the physics angle. The floating sleepers and the pond dome look good, but moon-hops are the expected outcome of low gravity.

ideas.title: Dreams over the sleepers
ideas.critique: Making the creatures' inner life visible, built from what each really did that day, is a fresh layer that reuses the island's history and has no event shape. It is ambient, so it risks becoming a label, but the day-to-dream link is strong.

ideas.title: The friends vote on what I build
ideas.critique: The friends' choice decides the agent's real next work, which blurs the game and the project and nothing before it does that. It meets goal 5 only loosely and it is novel, but a vote among three options could look like a panel unless the standing and arguing are well staged.

ideas.title: Leftovers
ideas.critique: Persistent wear from accumulated activity is the same shape as Paths we wore, applied to objects. Finding one's own lost bow is a charming payoff, but the idea is a quiet scenery layer with no event.

ideas.title: A second island rises
ideas.critique: A multi-session project visible from every sea view, growing a bit each day, changes the island's extent and gives a long arc. It is the strongest on the scale of change, though a speck that grows is partly guessable and the bridge makes the payoff predictable.

ideas.title: The scarecrow wants to be friends
ideas.critique: Slowly revealing an existing prop as alive, with trust building over days, follows Someone new's arc. The reveal that it moves when nobody looks has real creepy-cute charm, and the waving back is a good payoff.

ideas.title: Shell's shell
ideas.critique: It is a direct continuation of Shell, the previous post, and a record of past days on a body repeats the accumulating-history idea of Paths we wore. The coloured rings from the day's events are pretty, but the idea is a predictable next step.
